newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU envoy discusses peace process in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy discusses peace process in Egypt.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East peace envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos discussed the latest developments in the Middle East peace process with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Friday.
The EU appointed an envoy to the region in an attempt to play a greater role in talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
"We discussed the Syrian and the Lebanese tracks of the peace process as well as the future of the peace process as a whole," Moussa told reporters.
Moussa said Egypt, Syria and Saudi Arabia were coordinating on ways to boost negotiations.

Syria's Vice-President Abdel-Halim al-Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara toured several Arab countries, including Egypt and Saudi Arabia, in the past month in a bid to garner support for Damascus in its deadlocked talks with Israel.

Talks between Syria and Israel were halted last year while the Jewish state still had a Labour government in office. The main stumbling block in the negotiations was the Golan Heights, which Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war.
Negotiations have not resumed under right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government. Syria insists it will resume talks if they begin where the last round left off.
